outcome: Help regulated financial institutions prepare accurate, traceable reports faster by automating data mapping, validation, reconciliation, commentary, and control evidence.
overview: Regulatory reporting teams reconcile figures across finance, risk, treasury, actuarial and operational systems using large spreadsheets and manual controls, so rule changes, inconsistent definitions and weak lineage drive rework and key-person dependency. This solution maintains a governed reporting data model, maps authoritative sources to individual report cells, runs validation, reconciliation and prudential rules, explains period movements, enforces maker-checker workflow, and preserves evidence from source system to submission. Generative assistance drafts commentary only from validated figures with citations, and an accountable executive approves every report. An eight to twelve week proof of value targets one high-effort report, aiming at shorter preparation, fewer late adjustments, faster control testing and stronger audit confidence.

benefits.text: Reduce preparation and reconciliation effort on the selected report by a target 30–50%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target range to validate against the customer’s own measured cycle effort over two reporting cycles — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Provide cell-level lineage from source system to submitted figure for every scoped cell
benefits.source: Reference design — governed data layer and metadata capture, Redington BFSI catalogue
benefits.limits: Lineage is complete only for sources brought into scope; unmapped feeder systems remain manual

benefits.text: Cut late manual adjustments and control exceptions by a target 20%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on upstream data-quality ownership; adjustments caused by source close timing are outside the solution’s control

benefits.text: Reduce spreadsheet and key-person dependency by versioning every rule, mapping, commentary and approval
benefits.source: Reference design — versioned mappings and immutable evidence store, Redington BFSI catalogue
benefits.limits: Institutional knowledge still has to be captured into the rule set; the platform preserves it, it does not elicit it

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA), or hybrid with sensitive processing on customer-controlled infrastructure; reporting data and evidence remain within the customer tenancy and the regulator’s retention jurisdiction

notFor.situation: No authoritative source of record has been agreed for the figures in scope
notFor.why: Mapping cannot be governed if two systems both claim to be right; the platform would automate an unresolved dispute

notFor.situation: No reconciled historical cycles exist to run a parallel comparison against
notFor.why: A parallel run is the only honest acceptance test for a regulatory report; without prior submissions there is nothing to compare to

notFor.situation: The institution expects the system to approve or file the submission itself
notFor.why: Accountability for a regulatory submission is personal and non-delegable; the workflow requires named maker, checker and accountable approver

notFor.situation: Framework or taxonomy licensing rights for the target report are not held
notFor.why: Rule and taxonomy content cannot be encoded or distributed without the right to use it

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer’s accountable executives and report owners retain all approval and submission responsibility · Duration: 8–12 weeks to proof of value; a further 16–32 weeks to production depending on report scope and source quality
Delivery pod: Partner project lead + data lead, vendor platform specialist, reporting subject-matter expert; customer reporting sponsor, finance and risk owners, data stewards, compliance, internal audit, security, architecture and the accountable approver · Support model: Reporting-calendar aligned coverage with enhanced support around submission windows; severity-based response targets; partner first line with vendor escalation; optional managed controls
1) Discovery and effort baseline for the selected report
2) Report, source and control design
3) Data ingestion and mapping build
4) Rule and reconciliation testing
5) Workflow and output generation
6) Security testing and UAT
7) Parallel reporting cycle
8) Training and production launch
9) Stabilisation and handover
deliverables: Scoped figures reconcile to the prior submission within the agreed tolerance in the parallel run
Lineage and retrievable evidence complete for every scoped cell
Rule and output-format validation passed for the target framework version
Maker-checker segregation enforced with no route to generate a submission without recorded approvals
Security, retention and regulator-access requirements approved; preparers and reviewers trained and monitoring active
effort: 8–12 weeks to proof of value; a further 16–32 weeks to production depending on report scope and source quality
languages: English delivery and reporting interface; Arabic user support where required
